questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As i'm really interested in journalism, I chose UNSW in Sydney because in allowed me to choose multiple journalism courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UNSW did a really good job at giving all the needed information for studying abroad which made everything very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UNSW provided a really informative presentation when i first arrived, as well as emails and a very informative website.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was super lucky to find a place to live on via facebook with 5 other danish students three months before I landed in Sydney.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be very expensive, and I would highly recommend finding a place before you arrive. I know a few exchange students who ended up living in very expensive but poorly maintained apartments. Because the housing market in Sydney is so difficult, there are a lot of scams, and people take advantage of exchange students by charging them an obscene amount of rent for places that aren’t very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I became super lucky, but overall you are very much on your own and it is super expensive. There is housing on campus, but it is expensive and difficult to get.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a very very stressful process and I did not feel like I could get much help. To be fair, UNSW did provide multiple zoom meeting and mails about the registration process, but it was a very long process, and being on the other side of the planet while registration was super difficult - as every thing in UNSW system was new.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: zoom meetings and mails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did get 3 out of the 4 courses I wanted - but on UNSW website it was super challenging to understand which courses I was able to take - given the courses I had taken on KU. I took a lot of time, but when I first figured out which courses I was able to take, the process became a bit more smooth.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I takes A LOT OF TIME, so put time off to figure everything out

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was super lucky with the courses I ended up taking with super good teachers ! The classroom culture was very different from home, the students were a lot younger, and not super committed. People rarely showed up to class on time, did not pay much attention and rarely did the reading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The were much more casual and more personal I would say - they learned all of our names and very super engaged in our interests. Just as UCPH, UNSW did lectures and tutorial - forelæsninger og seminar.  People rarely showed up to the lectures as they were recorded and could therefore be seen from home. The lectures mostly consisted of class discussions - this was great when students were committed and interested and less great when people were not.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMM2000 Creating Social Change Summer, 2025
MDIA3097-Race, Media, Politics (T1 2025)
MDIA3002-News Analysis and Production (T1 2025)
DDES1040-Graphics and Print/Making - T1 2025

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: MDIA3002-News Analysis and Production (T1 2025) - the teachers were extremely experienced and provided really good knowledge.
